text:
Sean Gallagher: pulling a follow-up thread from yesterday’s PM (context gaps + slow triage). Main ask from leadership was: map actions -> collectors + make sure we don’t ship a bot that confidently lies.

Here’s my draft mapping (pls poke holes):
- “What changed?” in first 2–5 min -> Deploy collector (ENG-2842 / pr_0124)
- “Did routing/flags change?” -> Config diff collector (ENG-2843 / pr_0125)
- “Are we saturated / throttling / queueing?” -> Saturation snapshot (ENG-2844 / pr_0126 + obs dashboards pr_0321)
- “Bot spam / sensitive incidents” -> Posting controls + restricted mode (ENG-2847 / pr_0128, formatting pr_0127)
- “Correlate changes with graphs” -> annotation schema + dashboard overlay (ENG-2846 + redwood pr_18421 + pr_18452)

Open question: the ‘suspected change’ heuristic (pr_0132) — do we want this in MVP bundle or later?

:link: PM action list: https://confluence.redwood.example/postmortems/pm-2025-02-13#action-items

Rafael Mendes: +1 on mapping. For MVP I care most about (a) deploys, (b) effective config diff, (c) saturation snapshot, (d) links.

On suspected-change: I like the idea but the wording scares me. Responders will anchor HARD on whatever the bot highlights.

If we do it, it can’t say “suspected cause”. It should say something like “Potentially relevant recent change(s) near start of impact window (correlation only)”.

Aisha Bello: also remember we’re going to measure “time-to-suspect-change” as a metric. If the bot auto-suspects, we need to be careful not to game our own metric.

Maybe track:
- “time-to-first-change-evidence posted” (bot)
- “time-to-human-acknowledged-change” (reaction / button / slash cmd)

Otherwise MTTR reporting will look great while responders are actually being misled.

Logan Wright: from telemetry POV the heuristic is easy to make “look smart” by picking any change in a window.

The tricky bit is defining the window. If we default to “degradation started at t0” based on alert firing, we’re already noisy. Alert time != impact start.

If we do heuristics, the bot should:
- show the window it used (e.g., t0-30m to t0+10m)
- include the raw list anyway (not just the highlighted one)
- include a confidence label based on overlap + blast radius

Allison Grant: +1 to showing its work.

Also: we should ensure heuristics don’t become an excuse to skip saturation signals. A lot of incidents are “no change, just load + queue collapse”.

Would rather have the bot say:
- recent changes
- saturation snapshot
- “no changes detected in last X”

…and let the human decide.

Priya Natarajan: config diffs in particular can be misleading if we don’t resolve “effective config” correctly per region + tier.

Example: someone flips a flag in control plane, but it only affects dedicated pools in us-east, not hosted.

If suspected-change highlights a config delta without stating scope (service/region/cluster), it’ll cause bad rollbacks.

Ethan Park: on pr_0132 the current heuristic is basically:
1) pick start_time = first alert
2) find deploy/config events that overlap [start_time-30m, start_time+15m]
3) rank by “largest surface area”

I agree it’s too eager. We can gate with additional checks:
- require explicit region match (no global highlight)
- require error/latency change after event time (simple slope check)
- never highlight more than 1 deploy + 1 config change per service

But still feels risky for MVP.

Jacob Stein: FWIW responders in #incidents asked for “what changed” like 20 times in the last month. They want a short answer.

But I agree with everyone: the short answer can’t be “this caused it”.

Possible compromise: rename it to “Change candidates” and format it as:
- Candidate 1: deploy … (occurred 12m before alert)
- Candidate 2: routing policy … (occurred 7m before alert)

And then a line: “These are time-adjacent changes, not a root-cause claim.”

Marissa Cole: product POV: readability in Slack matters here.

If we add a ‘Change candidates’ section it must be:
- visually separate
- include timestamps relative to *impact* start (if we can compute) or alert time (if not)
- include a disclaimer in the header (not footnote)

Also we should give responders a quick way to mark it “useful / misleading”. Even a :thumbsup:/:thumbsdown: instruction is fine for V1.

Paula Mendes: +1 and would like it behind a flag initially.

We’ve seen this in other tooling: “suspected cause” turns into “truth” within ~2 mins.

If we do it, MVP should be:
- off by default
- enable only for SRE rotation first
- revisit after game day

Marcus Lin: security/compliance angle: heuristic + highlighting tends to increase the amount of metadata people paste into other channels.

Please make sure:
- links are to internal dashboards w/ auth
- no customer identifiers or request payload fragments ever appear in the highlighted line
- in restricted-mode incidents, the bot should not post the candidates list into #incidents at all (only into restricted channel)

If you need a review pass on wording for “restricted mode” output, loop me in.

Talia Benson: capturing decisions + next steps for the project plan.

Proposal (based on this thread):
1) MVP bundle includes deploy + config diff + saturation snapshot + links (no heuristic highlight)
2) ‘Change candidates’ (formerly suspected-change) is Phase 4, behind feature flag, SRE-only beta
3) Add explicit instrumentation: measure time-to-first-change-evidence vs time-to-human-acknowledged-change

If that’s right I’ll update ENG-2841 + create a subtask under ENG-2850 for rollout gating.

Sean Gallagher: aligns with what I’m hearing.

Let’s do:
- Keep the raw “Recent changes” list (deploy + config) in Phase 1/2, but no highlight.
- For Phase 4, we ship “Change candidates” behind flag w/ strict copy + scope rules.

Action items I’m taking:
- Update spec language: replace “suspected change” with “Change candidates (correlation-only)” + include ‘show your work’ (window + scope) (I’ll comment on pr_0132)
- Ask Jacob + Marissa to review Slack copy for the disclaimer header
- Add metric defs to the SLO impact doc (Aisha/Logan I’ll sync)

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: Works.

Can we also explicitly add to the spec that bot should say “No recent changes detected” when deploy/config collectors return empty? That’s valuable signal too.

Allison Grant: yes please. “empty” should be a first-class output, not a silent absence.

Incident Bot: (system) Noted feedback: treat empty collector output as an explicit section. 

Aisha Bello: I’ll draft the metric split and drop it into the SRE metrics doc:
- bot_bundle_latency_p95
- bot_bundle_partial_rate
- time_to_first_change_evidence
- time_to_human_ack_change
- MTTR by incident type (change-driven vs saturation-driven)

Will link here once up.

Priya Natarajan: for Phase 4 gating, we should require that config snapshot endpoint latency is stable. If snapshot calls are slow, we’ll end up with ‘Change candidates’ built on stale config and that’s worst-case.

Ethan Park: +1. We can add “config snapshot age” into the bundle (e.g., ‘effective config last updated 3m ago’). That helps responders trust/discount it.

Sean Gallagher: great call. That’s also a nice guardrail for later heuristics.

Talia Benson: updates I’m making in Linear:
- ENG-2841: note decision on deferring heuristic highlight
- ENG-2850: add task “Phase 4 change-candidates beta flag + copy review + restricted-mode behavior”

Will post links once done.

Marcus Lin: one more ask: for the disclaimer line, avoid words like “safe” or “not sensitive” (those get copy/pasted into incident comms). Just stick to “correlation-only” / “time-adjacent”.

Marissa Cole: ack. I’ll draft a compact header like:
“Change candidates (time-adjacent; correlation only — verify before rollback)”

And then keep the per-item lines short.

Sean Gallagher: perfect. Thanks all. Closing the loop once the spec + Linear updates are in.
